candidate.educational_objective: Explain the prokinetic effect of metoclopramide in diabetic gastroparesis.

options.A: Increased upper gastrointestinal motility with accelerated gastric emptying.
options.C: Permanent blockade of gastric acid production.
options.D: Formation of a protective ulcer coating over the duodenum.

candidate.rationale: Metoclopramide stimulates motility of the upper gastrointestinal tract, increases antral contractions and small-intestinal peristalsis, and accelerates gastric emptying and intestinal transit. These prokinetic effects support its use in diabetic gastroparesis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Metoclopramide increases upper-GI motility and accelerates gastric emptying.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology §12.1—stimulates upper-GI motility and accelerates gastric emptying
candidate.stem: A client with diabetic gastroparesis is prescribed metoclopramide. Which therapeutic effect should the nurse expect?
